intended_object: Given a linear functional f : A → R on an R-module A, the induced functional on the multiplicative opposite Aᵐᵒᵖ, x ↦ f(unop x) (from the docstring "Opposite-algebra version of a module dual functional" and the name).
explanation: The body is (unop R).toLinearMap ∘ₗ LinearMap.op f. In the library, LinearMap.op f sends x to op (f (unop x)) as a map Aᵐᵒᵖ →ₗ Rᵐᵒᵖ, and unop R is (MulOpposite.opLinearEquiv R).symm, here at type Rᵐᵒᵖ ≃ₗ[R] R. So f.op x = f (MulOpposite.unop x), which is exactly the intended functional on the opposite. It is stated for a commutative semiring R and an R-module A, which is the natural setting for duals; the star-algebra and quantum-set variables in scope are not used. Mathlib has no dedicated declaration for this. The same map is f ∘ₗ (MulOpposite.opLinearEquiv R).symm.toLinearMap, so this is a convenience name, not a narrower copy of a general construction.
